newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks mixed, LVMH sells Guinness shares.
newsitem.headline: French stocks mixed, LVMH sells Guinness shares.

text.p: French shares opened, slipped back somewhat, and recovered its gains on Friday, with LVMH making a big jump as traders said it was selling 135 million shares in Guinness Plc for around 414p per share.

Market sources said that LVMH, up 4.53 percent at 1,570, was selling Guinness shares in the market through Goldman Sachs in an operation which would reduce its stake to 15 percent from 21. LVMH had no comment.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 0.2 points or 4.77 percent at 2,412.54 at 0910 GMT.
LVMH later confirmed the sale of a seven percent stake.
Havas slipped 0.65 percent to 398.20, after a rise over the past two days on rumours in would buy out minorities from CEP Communication, following Havas's confirmation on Thursday evening.
Havas, which has a 74 percent stake, is spending 2.7 billion francs on buying out minorities at 470 francs per share. CEP, which was suspended on January 14 at 400 francs, remains suspended today.
AXA, down 0.58 percent at 345.50, said it will pre-pay a convertible bond for 3.65 billion and if all bonds were converted its 1997 net would be boosted by 180 million.
